qc_2_three_sisters_wall.blurb: Three Sisters' Wall is a short sector on the left side of the Lac Boisseau cliff, set beside a lake in the Laurentides near La Conception. Ten routes are listed, seven bolted sport lines and three trad lines. Grades run from the high 5.7s through 5.9 and cluster at 5.10, with a single 5.11, so it suits climbers working through the moderate range. Three cracks split the face. The climbs are fairly brief, some vertical and some slightly overhanging, and the rock can stay damp, so it climbs best after a dry stretch.

qc_c_lune_de_jour_couloir_1.blurb: This section sits where the trail meets the cliff on Pic aux Corbeaux, the gneiss crag in Mont-Orford provincial park in the Eastern Townships. A big roof here holds some of the hardest climbing nearby. The walk up from the parking lot is steep and takes about half an hour.

qc_g_bloc_choss_et_compagnie.blurb: A small cluster of ten bolted sport routes below the Grand Mur on Pic aux Corbeaux, in Mont-Orford provincial park. Most of the lines are on two huge boulders that the trail passes between, just before the main cliff base. Grades skew hard: one 5.10, a handful around 5.12, and the rest at 5.13 to 5.14, so it is mainly a stop for strong sport climbers. The flagship line goes up a face under a small roof next to the path. Most routes earn two or three stars, and the rock is gneiss.

qc_5_bob_s_wall.blurb: Bob's Wall is a ten-route sector at Mont Rigaud, west of Montreal, on the pink granite that makes up this small sport area. Seven routes are bolted sport lines and three are trad. The spread is wide, starting around 5.6 and 5.7 and stretching up to a few 5.12s and a single 5.13, with a handful in the middle at 5.8 to 5.11, so there is something for most leaders. Walls at Rigaud are typically 10 to 15 metres tall, and scattered trees give some summer shade after the sun leaves in the early afternoon.
